summary: Engine update: Swift's dives hit harder from height, with a height badge on stage.
Home screen polish: button labels centred and sized, burn button on one line.
Home screen redesign: a painted wooden bar with the menu, wallet Treats and run buttons.
Treats window now scrolls on small screens.
Get Treats inside the game: burn HOODOGE from the Treats window and a new HOW TO GET TREATS guide.
The Shop now opens on top of the outlaw picker when you jump to it from there.
Conker the Bombardier is here: a new outlaw who plants acorn bombs instead of swinging, with a full deck of his own and fresh art. Sherwood Club members can pick him up in the Shop.
The archer's arrows fly straight even mid-hop, and every one of her new cards now has its own strike.
The archer's card pool now matches the hound's, with new shots, footwork and close-quarters tricks, each with its own icon. Gold explains itself and the collection shows cards per outlaw.
Mystery choices now show their result, card draws are visible, the shopkeeper can be visited again, warnings read clearer, a miss sounds glum, and the collection lists cards per outlaw.
Attack strikes stay on screen a little longer before they fade.
Story stops now unfold over their full illustration, a dropped card sinks into the monster it was aimed at, and the rest of the hand holds still while you aim.
Every attack card now has its own strike: charges throw up dust, bites drip venom, barks ripple out, and the archer's arrows fly across the field before they land.
Connecting a wallet from a phone browser now keeps the game where it is: the wallet app only approves and signs, then hands you back.
A card you drag onto a monster or your outlaw turns see-through so you can still see what is underneath.
Story stops that cost or restore health now show your current and maximum health beside the choices.
Every monster now walks in on the new outlaw, being backed into a corner stings the same from start to finish, and the rest-stop preview shows what a reworded improvement does.
Picking the new outlaw right after connecting a wallet works again.
The outlaw picker shows the new Club outlaw in full colour before a wallet is connected, with the lock on the badge alone.
The second outlaw is open to Sherwood Club members, and the picker now re-reads a wallet's standing instead of trusting an old sign-in.
Groundwork for the next outlaw: she keeps her distance, the monsters close in, and her cards and icons are in place behind the coming-soon sign.
The phone menu now scrolls, so every link and the theme switch are reachable on smaller screens.
Two of the upcoming Sherwood Club outlaws got their redrawn portraits, and the victory screen now fits on short phone screens.
The outlaw picker now shows which newcomers are for club members and lets you connect or disconnect your wallet right there.
Three new outlaws step onto the roster with their portraits, marked coming soon while their cards are forged.
Three new outlaws are on the roster for club members, waiting on their portraits, and monsters now roll their luck on every single hit.
One of the trinkets now also keeps you out of surprise fights, so it earns its slot.
Drag a card onto a monster to play it, status chips that are always visible, and a tidier battle stage.
Another balance pass on cards and trinkets, so strong picks come with a real cost.
Runs in progress now survive game updates and finish on the rules they started with, plus reward screens that always fit.
A big balance pass on cards so every pick costs more thought, and early fights that no longer repeat the same foe.
Sherwood Outlaw is now linked from the site, and the roadmap marks it as shipped.
Tougher mid-run challengers that each push back on a different habit, plus small readability fixes and an art touch-up.
A long-term challenge for players who keep winning, more varied monster behaviour, map surprises that can now go wrong, a wide balance pass, and a larger, cleaner layout on phones.

Tester feedback pass: bleed is capped and some foes shrug it off, long fights make every monster angrier, standing behind a wall no longer carries over, and almost every card is open from the first run.
How-to-play in eleven languages, a confirm step before taking a reward card, fewer trinkets per run, and a tougher luck draw for the other side.
Two full practice runs on the live game, and the trinket shelf now makes room when it fills up.
Bigger packs that hit softer, a final fight that calls for help, a trader behind some question marks, and a lighter first load.
Rank bundles now climb in power: early ranks round out your deck, the top ranks hold the strongest cards. The big haul after each act's final fight fits on one page again.
Resting at the fire now heals less, so sharpening a card is the better call when you are healthy; a few upgrades were evened out as well.
Twenty-three new cards and twelve new trinkets, each with its own art, including cards that belong to two styles at once.
Four deck styles now hold up on their own: Brawler and Chomp got stronger, Zoomies and Guard Dog were trimmed, and the game offers you more of whatever style your deck is leaning toward.
The battle screen no longer shifts sideways and cuts off its left edge, and tapping the hand right as a fight ends is handled quietly.
A run no longer starts silently when the server cannot be reached; a clear message asks you to try again. Rest-stop choices now fit the screen and the bounty strip is readable.
Beating the Bear King now ends with a single draw that adds a luck card to your deck for good, and the score screen shows the Treats you earned, now two per gold coin left.
The starting luck deck is calmer now: mostly plain cards with a single plus one, so the earned cards from the Bear King matter more. The tutorial also explains the luck card after your first attack.
Music and sound effect volume sliders, pinch-zoom on the map, and lighter backgrounds for phones that were crashing in Safari.
The luck pile now carries over between fights, the drawn card flips open large before the attack lands, and a top-right pill shows cards left out of the whole deck.
Your growth now follows your wallet: connect it on any device and your luck deck, poster and collection are all there, with nothing lost.
Every attack now draws a luck card, for you and for the monsters, and winning the final fight grows your deck for good. Chests let you choose, and a first balance pass evens out the four play styles.
After a win, picking your card takes you straight back to the map. How to Play now explains the card badges.
The mid-battle map view is back, and the trail markers are smaller and tighter.
A full sound pack replaces the code-made tones: every tap, swipe, hit and reward has its own layered sounds, and the music dips under the victory and defeat stings.
The monster introduction now appears at the top of the battle, out of the way of your cards.
Disconnect your wallet right from the Shop or the Treats window.
A Treats window on the title screen: see what you earned, what your wallet holds, and claim with one tap when it qualifies.

Treats earned in the game now move onto a wallet only for HOODOGE holders above a set amount or Sherwood Origins NFT owners; everything earned stays safe until then, and How to Play explains the rule.
The WANTED poster got its painted look: parchment, lettering, rank seals and a HOODOGE mugshot. The settings gear is easier to spot.
A new way to grow your collection: every run adds to your WANTED poster, and one shopkeeper now keeps something special under the counter. Stage characters stand closer to the ground.
New painted backdrops for the after-battle and treasure screens, and two keepsake icons redrawn to match the rest.
HOODOGE now wears the key-art look in battle, a proper gear opens settings from the title screen, and the top bar hints when it has more to show.
Roadmap updated with Sherwood Outlaw, coming soon.
Hoodoge's arrow now flies forward from his bow when you click him.
Bigger map view with smaller, tidier markers.
Rewritten How to Play, Home and Community links on the title screen, shop text fixes.
Layout now renders the same in Firefox as in Chrome.
Cleaner map icons; tougher encounters are now called Bounties.
Free cosmetics for Sherwood Origins holders.
Much longer journeys on a scrolling map, with the balance kept where it was.
Character select added before each run, with more outlaws on the way.
Shop scene reworked so everything fits on one screen.
See what you get before you choose in the store and at rest stops; pinch zoom works again on phones.
Mascot updated to the HOODOGE logo character.
Shorter, faster rounds.
Clearer guidance when getting Treats.
Pause button and a new sound toggle.
Smoother wallet connection on phones.
Match-pop effects shop with an in-game Treats checkout.
Play under a name with or without a wallet; holder badges shown next to names.
New start menu with a How to Play guide.
Round pacing reworked; daily mode retired.
GitHub link added to the header and community links; the top bar now fits small phones.
Mobile play improvements.
In-game cosmetic shop opened.
Leaderboard and player record improvements.
Progression and collection features added.
Combat readability and feedback improvements; new sound set.
New title screen and map art.
Sherwood Outlaw is live: a HOODOGE card game with a global leaderboard.
Stonk Detector moved into the main site.
Buyback & burn page live.
One Treats balance shared across all HOODOGE products.
Hoodoge Pop is live: a quick HOODOGE puzzle game.
Original soundtrack added.
New scene, character poses and ambient motion.
